phenomenon.what: Text placed in a manuscript to instruct an automated (LLM-assisted) peer reviewer, rendered invisible to a human reader by setting the foreground colour equal to the background - white on white - or by a near-zero font size.
phenomenon.source: Zhicheng Lin, 'Hidden Prompts in Manuscripts Exploit AI-Assisted Peer Review', Communications of the ACM 69(7):53-56, DOI 10.1145/3779116; preprint arXiv:2507.06185. https://cacm.acm.org/opinion/hidden-prompts-in-manuscripts-exploit-ai-assisted-peer-review/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06185

disclosure.headline: 'Positive review only': Researchers hide AI prompts in papers
disclosure.population_named_by_disclosure: 18 papers found on arXiv as of 2025-07-07 across authors in Asia, North America and Europe (Lin/CACM). This work follows a 5-paper cohort tracked by the sibling practice The Field, not the whole population.

cohort_source.caveat_carried: Floor estimate. The Field records that arXiv search does not reliably index invisible PDF text, so actual occurrence may be higher; the cohort is five tracked papers, not the full population.
